title: Find story words by their concentration
statement: To catch a question that needs a story detail not yet read, track only words concentrated in at most two of the collection's texts, measured from the texts themselves.
detail: A forward-reference checker for Grade 3 narrative lessons flags a question, option, hint or feedback line that depends on a concrete story noun the child has not read yet. It builds a document-frequency table over every lesson's passages, so a word found across many stories counts as general vocabulary and only words concentrated in one or two stories are tracked, measured from the file rather than a hand-written list. It skips the preview pages before a lesson's first passage, which were its largest source of false alarms on approved lessons.
against: It tracks named things only: "It will not catch a forward dependency on an unnamed fact" (grade3-reading/curriculum-gen/checks/KNOWN-LIMITS.md lines 61-62). It was never calibrated for expository Grade 5 lessons, where it reports 10 findings and every one checked was mechanically false (same file, lines 69-70), and none of the sources read records a real defect it caught on approved content. It skips the preview pages before a lesson's first passage, yet a separate case study found a pre-reading vocabulary check that gave away a story's ending and calls for a chronology audit of every pre-reading example and checkpoint (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans-wiki/Peter-Pan-Quality-Case-Study-2026-08-24.md`, lines 134 and 145).

evidence.quote: A question, option, feedback or hint on page N must not depend on a concrete story noun the child has not read yet: one whose first passage appearance is on a page AFTER N, or which appears in no passage of the lesson at all.
Only words concentrated in one or two stories can be story nouns. This is measured from the file, not guessed from a hand-written list.
pages before the lesson's first passage are not checked for forward reference. Checking them was this rule's single largest false-positive source on the approved lessons.
A pre-reading vocabulary check disclosed the story’s ending.
Chronology audit for every pre-reading example and checkpoint
